attributes.nuance_translation: A polite expression used for directly inviting someone to do (A).

attributes.body:
ませんか (or ないか more casually) is an expression that is used after verbs as an invitation. It basically translates to 'won't you do (A) with me?'.

This expression is a little bit different to ましょうか, in that it sounds directly like an invitation to do (A). ましょうか tends to sound more like a suggestion that (A) should be done.

It is recommended to use the ませんか version, as ないか would be a bit too casual to use with someone that you are not very close with (and is also technically not correct Japanese).

To make it clearer that the speaker wants to do (A) 'with' someone, expressions like 一緒（いっしょ）に 'together' are often added, for clarification.

To examine the difference between ましょうか and ませんか, let's have a look at how the nuance changes in the same type of sentence.

Here, ませんか will come across as an invitation due to the fact that you are asking the person if they 'wouldn't mind doing (A)' with you. This is the main reason that it is considered a more polite option when inviting someone to do something, than ましょうか.

ませんか is a polite way to extend an invitation, similar to 'Won't you…?' or 'Wouldn't you like to...?' in English. In contrast, たらどう has a stronger tone and is used to suggest or advise a course of action. For example, 何か食べませんか？ is a polite offer (e.g. to a guest), while 何か食べたらどう？ implies the speaker thinks the listener should eat something.

first_relatable.title: ませんか
first_relatable.meaning: Won't you, Would you not, Why don't we

second_relatable.title: たらどう
second_relatable.meaning: Why don't you...?, What if you did...?

attributes.body: ませんか is a polite way to extend an invitation, similar to 'Wouldn't you like to...?' in English. For example, 何か食べませんか？ ('Won't you eat something?') might be used when politely offering food to a guest. Note that unlike English, the たい form ('Do you want to…?') isn't typically used to invite someone in Japanese—何か食べたいですか？ simply asks if the person wants to eat something.

first_relatable.title: ませんか
first_relatable.meaning: Won't you, Would you not, Why don't we

attributes.body: ましょう and ませんか are both polite expressions based on the ます form that can be used to make suggestions or invitations. ましょう is more assertive and usually implies the speaker and listener will do something together (e.g., 食べましょう = 'Let's eat'). In contrast, ませんか is more of an invitation directed at the listener (e.g., 食べませんか = 'Won't you eat [some]?').

second_relatable.title: ませんか
second_relatable.meaning: Won't you, Would you not, Why don't we

attributes.body: ましょう and ませんか are both polite forms based on the ます form and used to make suggestions or invitations. ましょう typically suggests doing something together (e.g. 食べましょう = 'Let's eat'), while ませんか invites the listener to join (e.g. 食べませんか = 'Won't you eat [some]?') ましょう is more assertive, while ませんか is softer and more inviting.
